```sql
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           ol.order_id,
           pv.id                       AS variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)            AS qty,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents)    AS rev,
           GROUPING(ol.order_id)       AS g_order
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((pv.product_id, ol.order_id),
                             (pv.product_id, pv.id))
),
per_product AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*)  FILTER (WHERE g_order = 0)          AS order_count,
           (sum(qty) FILTER (WHERE g_order = 0))::bigint AS quantity,
           sum(rev)  FILTER (WHERE g_order = 0)          AS revenue_cents,
           count(*)  FILTER (WHERE g_order = 1)          AS variant_count
      FROM agg
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       pp.order_count,
       pp.quantity,
       pp.revenue_cents,
       pp.variant_count
  FROM per_product pp
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pp.product_id
 ORDER BY pp.quantity DESC, pp.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De twee `count(DISTINCT ...)` dwongen een sortering op (p.id, o.id) af. Die sortering liep met een external merge naar schijf. Ik vervang ze door één hash-gebaseerde GROUPING SETS-aggregatie: per (product, order) en per (product, variant) wordt één rij gemaakt, en het tellen van die rijen geeft exact dezelfde distinct-aantallen, terwijl de sommen uit de order-set komen. De `products`-join gebeurt pas na de aggregatie op ongeveer 1.750 rijen, en de `::bigint`-cast houdt het type van `quantity` gelijk aan het origineel.
